items.item_text: Pharmacy Technician license issued by the California State Board of Pharmacy.

Employment in this position is contingent upon successful completion of a Department of Justice (DOJ) Live Scan background check, verification and continued monitoring or licensure as it applies to the position, and successful completion of our background review or credentialing process, as appropriate to the position.

Experience with administrative and clerical tasks such as order supplies and equipment, developing reports and tracking logs.
Pharmacy Technician experience in a college health or university setting.
Proven computer experience and accurate data entry skills.
A minimum of 5 years of experience as a Pharmacy Technician.
Minimum of two years of experience in an ambulatory care pharmacy setting.

Under the general supervision of the Pharmacy Manager and Staff Pharmacist, the Pharmacy Technician III assists in all technical aspects of prescription filling and dispensing activities that are within the scope of their license under the California Board of Pharmacy. Duties include processing, filling and dispensing prescriptions, data entry of medications and prescriptions, understanding of UC Irvine SHIP insurance benefits (formulary, alternatives, etc.) as well as inventory management.
Must be able to demonstrate proper aseptic techniques.

This position’s schedule is M-F and during traditional work hours, however, weekend or non-traditional work hours may be required for special projects or busy times of the year, or when strict deadlines must be met. In the case of extended hours, this position may be required to work those hours.
Able to verbally communicate with patients to provide information and education regarding medication usage.

The employee must comply with OSHA, CA/OSHA, and CDC recommendations and requirements regarding vaccination and testing of healthcare employees. This includes, but may not be limited to; current hepatitis B immunizations, annual flu vaccinations, and annual tuberculosis screening. The employee must comply with CDPH and UC COVID-19 Vaccine Policy, by providing proof of Full Vaccination or submitting a request for Exception.
Maintain a work pace appropriate to the workload.
Per the UC Ethics Briefing, the employee is responsible for reporting any and all potential conflicts of interest to their supervisor in a timely manner.
Completion of a recognized and accredited Pharmacy Technician training program.
Knowledge of CA State and all Federal laws, rules and regulations governing the storage and dispensing of prescription drugs.
Bilingual skills to communicate effectively with patients.
General knowledge of the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).
Knowledge of UC policy and procedures for ordering pharmaceutical drugs.
Knowledge of drug formularies and prescription fee schedule.
Knowledge of Pharmacy terminology and calculations.
Knowledge of pharmacy reporting and inventory procedures.
Thorough understanding of drug categories, metric system and medical terminology.
Knowledge of generic and brand names of drugs and understand the use restrictions that apply.

Problem-solving skills to independently recognize and define a problem; identify the resources available to help solve the problem; create and implement viable solutions; and follow through to ensure the problem is resolved to the satisfaction of all parties.
Must be able to work in a collaborative manner and have strong interpersonal skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Must demonstrate customer service skills appropriate to the job.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships across the Health system.
Ability to use good judgment in responding to or referring questions by nurses, physicians, and other professional personnel.
Ability to work under constant interruptions.
Working knowledge of using an electronic medical record (EMR).
Working knowledge of Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, etc.).
